Stop a second copy of Cindy from overwriting the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
Cindy saves its whole client list after every command. With two copies
open on the same data file, a command in the older copy, even help,
overwrote the changes saved by the newer one, so deleted clients came
back and workout plan updates were lost.

Lock a file next to the data file when Cindy starts. If another copy
holds the lock, show an error and close without reading or saving any
file. If the lock cannot be taken for another reason, such as a folder
that cannot be written to, start without it as before.

Mention this in the user guide, and add a manual test to the developer
guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say when an appointment date or time does not exist
commitResults.messageBody:
A date such as 2027-02-29 or a time such as 24:00 is already in the
right format, but was rejected with the format message, so users looked
for a formatting mistake that was not there.

Keep the format message for input in the wrong format, and say that the
date or time is not real otherwise.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject past appointment dates and cancelling past appointments
commitResults.messageBody:
Appointments are for upcoming sessions, but appointment --add and
--reschedule accepted any date, such as 2020-01-01, without warning,
and appointment --cancel cancelled appointments that had already
happened.

Reject a first or new date before today, and refuse to cancel an
appointment dated before today. An appointment that has passed can
still be rescheduled to a new date. Today is read from a clock when the
command runs, as in list --today, so tests use a fixed date.

Update the user guide, and move its examples to dates that are not in
the past.

commitResults.messageTitle: Limit appointment dates to a year ahead and supported weeks
commitResults.messageBody:
appointment --add and --reschedule accepted any date, so a series from
9999-12-31 ran into year +10000, and appointment --week 9999-12-31
showed a week ending in +10000-01-02. No command accepts such dates as
input, so these appointments could not be listed or moved again.

Reject a first or new date more than one year after today, and reject
--week when its Monday to Sunday goes outside 0000-01-01 to 9999-12-31.
Viewing a single day with --date is unchanged.

Update the user guide to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix the advice for a reschedule clash in the user guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide said to cancel the other appointment when rescheduling
clashes with it. A cancelled appointment keeps its date and time, so
the reschedule still fails with the same clash.

Say that the other appointment has to be moved to a different date or
time first, and that this makes it active again if it was cancelled.

commitResults.messageTitle: Give each client a unique ID
commitResults.messageBody:
Clients can only be identified by their position in the displayed list,
which changes whenever the list is filtered, sorted or edited. Commands
that act on a specific client need a way to refer to the same client
every time.

Let's give each client a unique ID when it is added. The address book
keeps track of the next ID to give out and never reuses an ID, even
after the client it belonged to is deleted. IDs are saved in the data
file together with the next ID, and clients in data files saved before
IDs existed are given IDs in file order when the file is loaded.

AddressBook equality now also depends on the next person ID, but no
test checks equals or hashCode directly.

Let's add a test that covers both, including two address books that
differ only in their next person ID.

commitResults.messageTitle: Choose clients by ID or name in view, edit and delete
commitResults.messageBody:
The view, edit and delete commands choose a client by their position in
the displayed list, which changes whenever the list is filtered or
sorted. They also use a different argument style from add, which uses
--name and --phone.

Let's make these commands choose a client with --id ID or --name NAME
instead, and show each client's ID on their card in place of their list
position. A name chooses the client whose name contains it, ignoring
case. If several clients match, the command does not act on any of
them, but lists them and asks the user to choose one by ID. The new
values for edit use --to-name and --to-phone, so that they cannot be
confused with the --name used to choose the client.

The choosing logic is kept in PersonSelector and PersonTargetedCommand,
so that other commands acting on one client can reuse it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update UG and DG for client IDs and --id and --name
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG and DG describe view, edit and delete as choosing a client by
their position in the displayed list, using n/ and p/ for new values,
and do not mention client IDs at all.

Let's explain client IDs, the --id and --name arguments, what happens
when a name matches several clients, and the --to-name and --to-phone
arguments of edit. The use cases, glossary and manual testing steps are
updated to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify ID reuse after clear and the clients searched by selectors
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG and DG say that a client ID is never given to another client,
but clear resets the ID numbering, so the next client added after it
gets ID 1. The UG also does not say that --id and --name search all
clients, even when find shows only some of them.

Let's state that clear starts the ID numbering again, both where IDs
are introduced and in the clear section, and that --id and --name
search all clients, with an example after find.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find clients by name, phone number or ID
commitResults.messageBody:
The find command only accepts whole words of a client's name, in a
different style from the other commands, and cannot find clients by
phone number. Errors in commands also show only the problem, not the
format of the command, so users must look up the correct format.

Let's make find take --name, --phone and --id, any of which can be
combined, with names and phone numbers matched when they contain the
given text. The same phone matching lets commands choose a client by
--phone. Every input error of find, view, edit and delete now also
shows the format of the command.

NameContainsKeywordsPredicate is no longer used, so it is removed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a note, active status and tags to each client
commitResults.messageBody:
Clients only have a name, phone number and ID, so there is nowhere to
keep a note about a client, to record whether they still train with
the trainer, or to label them, e.g. as a gym or personal client.

Let's give each client a note, an active status and a set of tags,
save them in the data file, and show the tags and an Inactive label on
client cards and the note on the client details page. Clients in data
files saved without these details have no note, are active and have
no tags, so existing data files still load.

Commands to change these details are added separately.

Clients can now be inactive, but there is no command to mark them so.
Former or paused clients therefore cannot be told apart from clients
the trainer currently trains.

Let's add inactive and active commands that mark a client, chosen by
--id, --name or --phone, as inactive or active. Inactive clients keep
all their details and stay in the list, labelled as inactive, so that
they can be made active again later.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tag command for gym and personal clients
commitResults.messageBody:
Clients can now have tags, but there is no command to label a client
as a gym or a personal client, so the trainer cannot keep the two
client bases apart.

Let's add a tag command that labels a client, chosen by --id or
--name, with --type gym or --type personal. A client is either a gym
or a personal client, so setting one type replaces the other, while
any other tags of the client are kept. The two types are defined in
Tag, so that the custom tag groups planned by the team can build on
them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add note command to give a client a note
commitResults.messageBody:
Clients can now have a note, but there is no command to set it, so a
trainer cannot record context such as a client's injuries.

Let's add a note command that replaces the note of a client chosen by
--id or --name. As agreed by the team, the note must be in double
quotes, and an empty note removes it. The client's details page opens
afterwards, so that the trainer can see the note.
Find clients by name, phone number or ID

commitResults.messageTitle: Treat empty entries in data file as invalid
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file with an empty entry in a client's tag list, or in the
client list, makes Cindy crash with a NullPointerException on startup.
Only IllegalValueException is handled as invalid data, so the usual
fallback of starting with an empty address book is skipped.

Let's report such empty entries as invalid data, so that Cindy starts
as it does for any other invalid data file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show a complete command when several clients match
commitResults.messageBody:
When a name or phone number matches several clients, the message
suggests running the command again with --id, e.g. edit --id 2. For
commands that need more arguments, such as edit, the suggested command
leaves them out, so following the suggestion fails.

Let's let each command add its other arguments to the suggestion, so
that it is a complete command, e.g. edit --id 2 --to-phone "91234567".

Let's include the note in the suggested command, e.g.
note --id 2 --note "Knee injury".

commitResults.messageTitle: Stop client IDs from overflowing at the int limit
commitResults.messageBody:
A client ID of 2147483647 has no next ID, because the next ID would
overflow. Loading such a client, or adding one when the next ID is
2147483647, threw an uncaught exception: Cindy crashed on startup, or
added the client to the list without saving it and then rejected every
later add.

Let's keep 2147483647 free as the next ID after the largest client ID.
Client IDs now go up to 2147483646, a data file with a larger ID is
treated as invalid, and add shows an error once every ID has been used.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match names and phone numbers consistently
commitResults.messageBody:
Names were matched by lowercasing both sides with String#toLowerCase,
which turns a capital I with a dot above into an i followed by a
combining dot. So --name ipek did not match a client named İpek, even
though Name#equals already treats the two names as the same.

Phone numbers were matched as text, so --phone +65 missed clients whose
numbers were saved without a +, although the UG says phone searches
only look at the digits.

Let's match names with the same case folding as Name#equals, and
compare phone numbers by their digits only.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow find to search for clients in several groups
commitResults.messageBody:
find accepted only one --group, so there was no way to find clients in
two groups at once, such as gym clients in the morning group, since
gym and personal are searched with --group as well.

Let's accept --group more than once and find the clients in all of the
given groups. The UG now also says that a leading + is ignored in
--phone, matching the previous commit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix find syntax in command history examples
commitResults.messageBody:
The command history examples in the UG and DG still use find Alice and
find Bob, which find now rejects because it needs a filter such as
--name.

Let's use find --name Alice and find --name Bob instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let users copy a client's note to edit it
commitResults.messageBody:
note replaces the whole note, but the note on the client's details page
could not be selected or copied. To change one sentence of a long note,
users had to retype all of it.

Let's add a Copy note item when right-clicking the note, which copies
the note as it would be typed in a note command, with \n for each line
break, so it can be pasted into a new note command and changed.
LongFormText#toTypedText now does this conversion for both the copy and
the suggested commands that already wrote line breaks as \n.

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct note and view details in the guides
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG said a note cannot contain text that looks like a parameter,
such as --id, but text inside the quotes is kept as part of the note.
The DG view use case said every command that changes clients returns
to the client list, but commands that update the client's note,
workout plan or appointments keep showing the client's details.

Let's correct both, and describe how to copy a note in the UG.

commitResults.messageTitle: Simplify client creation to name and phone
commitResults.messageBody:
Adding a client requires email and address details inherited from the
original address book workflow. These fields are not needed for the
client roster and make client creation unnecessarily cumbersome.

Require only a client's name and phone number when adding them. Keep
legacy fields internally for storage compatibility.

Client contact input accepts inconsistent spacing and phone numbers of
arbitrary length. This can create duplicate-looking names and invalid
contact details.

Normalize whitespace in names and phone numbers, and require phone
numbers to contain exactly eight digits.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store only client names and phone numbers
commitResults.messageBody:
New clients use placeholder email and address values because the inherited
Person model and JSON adapter require legacy fields. This stores data
users never provided and exposes it in view and delete output.

Remove email, address, and tags from the client model, storage, edit
flow, and UI. Ignore legacy JSON properties so existing files remain
readable.

Client names and phone numbers need to support international formats while remaining consistent for storage and comparison.

Accept long-form add flags, normalize names and phone numbers, enforce the documented validation boundaries, and update the user guide and tests.
Exercise unquoted and mismatched-quote add arguments and verify the hash code contract for equal clients.

Contacts with the same name can represent different clients, but
name-only identity prevents those records from coexisting.

Compare normalized names and phone numbers for duplicate identity.
Warn when another client already uses the phone number.

Update tests and documentation for the new behavior.

commitResults.messageBody:

session documentation describes records as scheduled appointments.

These inconsistencies mislead users and allow duplicate clients.

Reject unsupported parameters and trailing text with usage guidance.

the entered country-code format for display. Update the guides and
add regression tests for argument errors and phone matching.

warnings so both input formats receive consistent treatment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep client profiles open after session updates
commitResults.messageBody:
Session add and edit commands return only feedback, causing the UI
to return to the client list after a successful update.

Session records are visible in the profile, so trainers must reopen
it to check each change. This differs from note and plan updates.

Return the updated client with the command result so the UI displays
the latest profile immediately. Cover this behavior in session tests
and update the user guide, developer guide and in-app help.

Reuse the existing profile result mechanism to keep session updates
consistent with other commands that display the updated client.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify that clearing deletes clients and groups
commitResults.messageBody:
Clearing removes custom groups as well as clients, but the confirmation
prompt and guides only describe client deletion. Trainers can lose their
group setup without warning.

Describe group deletion in the command messages, Help and User Guide.
Explain that custom groups need recreating while built-in client types
remain available, and check that the prompt warns before changing data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Protect unreadable client data during startup
commitResults.messageBody:
An unreadable data file produces an empty client model. The next command
can save that model over the original file without a visible warning.

Stop startup before creating command logic when client data cannot load.
Show the file location and recovery instructions in an error dialog, then
close Cindy while preserving the original file.

Check rejection of corrupt data, recovery after repair, safe shutdown and
the visible error dialog. Update the User Guide to explain recovery.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep client IDs visible when names wrap
commitResults.messageBody:
Long client names widen list cards and push IDs and inactive status out
of view. Fixed-height rows also leave too little space for wrapped names.

Size list cells to the viewport and allow names to shrink and wrap while
reserving space for IDs and status. Let row heights grow with their cards.

Check long inactive names at default and minimum content widths, visible
IDs and status, phone placement, and the absence of horizontal scrolling.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reset profile scrolling when switching clients
commitResults.messageBody:
Opening another client retains the previous profile scroll position, so
the new client header and the start of their details can be out of view.

Reset vertical scrolling when the displayed client ID changes. Preserve
scrolling when updating the same client so edits do not jump to the top.

Check profile switching, same-client updates and navigation through the
main window command dispatcher.

The legacy tag selector overrides the main theme, leaving tags with the
older color and rectangular shape.

with wider padding so tags match the green pill design.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bundle Noto Sans Mono for command input
commitResults.messageBody:
The command font depends on fonts installed on each computer and does
not provide the requested Noto Sans Mono appearance.

Bundle the regular Google Fonts face and its SIL Open Font License.
Load it through a resource stream so paths containing spaces work, and
apply it to command input. Check the font selected by the rendered field.

commitResults.messageTitle: Prevent overlapping cards at the end of the list
commitResults.messageBody:
The list can estimate a short row below its card minimum height. At the
bottom of the list, that places adjacent cards too close together.

the full card. Check adjacent cards after scrolling to the final client
at two widths and four heights.

Long-form command input converts every backslash followed by a lowercase
n into a line break. The guides do not explain that another backslash
does not escape this sequence, or that re-entering stored text can change
its contents.

Explain these limitations in the User Guide with examples and link them
from the command-format and data-file guidance. Describe storage
preservation and command conversion in the Developer Guide so that the
documented limitation reflects the existing behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Restore client data when saving fails
commitResults.messageBody:
A save failure leaves command changes in memory, allowing a later
successful write to persist a clear that previously reported an error.

Restore the previous client data when saving fails. Preserve clients,
custom groups and the next client ID, and cover later successful saves
with regression tests.

commitResults.messageBody:

without write access. Keep confirmed clearing dependent on persistence.
